ideas.title: The friends are the battery
ideas.goal: The player lures friends into a line with berries; each carries a kiln-fired pot cell on its back, joined to the next by a real copper cord, and the motor at the end of the line winds a rope that hauls a basket of berries up from the beach for them. Every friend that steps in makes the winch faster; a bored one wanders off to fish, its cord pulls out of the clip, the circuit opens and the basket stops halfway. The friends keep the motor going because they want what it brings.
ideas.toward: The road's cell step, honest (Fe | brine || CuSO4 | Cu, 0.78 V, a pot wall of 1-3 Ohm like the porous-pot Daniell cells of the 1840s: 0.05-0.15 W each, where sea water gave 1.5 mW), plus the first machine friends power and want; the cart will need the same cells and the same friends.
ideas.idea: No switch anywhere: the cords are rods (hotrod.jl XPBD) whose ends are clipped to the pots' copper and iron terminals; circuit.jl builds the network from which conductor touches which (contact spots, Holm resistance), so series or parallel is wherever the cords actually reach, and a cord that comes taut as a friend walks away pulls out of its clip by the force on it. Friends walk to the berries by their own gait and needs (no teleport); Lumi nudges with its beak. Each pot: Nernst emf, limiting current n F D C / delta, Faraday's law moving copper (the blue thins, the plate pinkens) checked against measured Daniell-cell figures. The winch: the drum motor's torque from the field solve against the basket's weight on a 1 cm drum through a stick-and-cord reduction; 6 pots lift a 1 kg basket at a few cm/s. Watcher sees, filmed along the line at the friends' height: pony-sized friends with terracotta pots, copper cords looping between them, the copper rotor spinning at the end and the berry basket rising up the post, then stopping when Pickles walks off to the pier.
ideas.form: A plugin at the beach below the motor bench (Jump in: carry berries to lure, beak-nudge a friend, clip a cord); a traced film framed on the line of friends with the rising basket.

ideas.title: A kite pulls the cart across the wet sand
ideas.goal: Lumi sits on the front of the wooden cart with two kite lines in its feet, the friends climb on behind, and the player steers a big leaf kite: hold it overhead and the cart barely creeps; swoop it in figure-eights across the wind and the cart surges along the wet sand at the waterline, ruts behind; swing too hard on a turn and the cart tips a wheel up and the friends lean. Over the dry sand it bogs down. A skill toy you get better at, with friends aboard.
ideas.toward: The cart itself, built now: frame, axle, wheels of a chosen width rolling in sand (wheelsand.jl, done), friends' masses aboard, the first ride; and the crosswind kite is the wind engine the road needs (later its line drum turns the generator). George Pocock's charvolant pulled a carriage with kites at 20 mph in 1826.
ideas.idea: Kite: a rigid sail with lift and drag from its angle of attack (glider.jl's thin-plate coefficients), two lines whose length difference rolls and steers it (real two-line steering), tethers of segments with weight and drag, the apparent wind of a crosswind swoop (pull grows with its square: a 4 m2 kite in 6 m/s wind gives ~100 N downwind, ~900 N in figure-eights). Cart: rigid frame and wheels, each wheel's sinkage, slip and side force from the Wong-Reece soil model per step; wet sand at the waterline (firmer: a soil from Wong's tables) against dry sand above it; friends as masses from their mesh volume, so where they sit decides when it tips. Watcher sees a bright kite carving eights over the sea, the lines taut, the cart with three friends running along the surf line throwing up wet sand, and a hard turn lifting a wheel.
ideas.form: A playable plugin on the beach (Jump in: left/right steer the kite, friends board), a traced film along the surf line at the friends' height.
